research_question: Develop a generalized additive model (GAM) with a cubic regression spline to approximate the stage-discharge rating curve using long-term discrete field measurements, while accounting for and filtering out ice-affected data.

phase_1.user_prompt: I am researching how stage-discharge relationships (rating curves) evolve over time due to channel changes, using the Pere Marquette River at Scottville, Michigan as a case study site. To get started, I need the official USGS site number for this streamgage, as well as the standard 5-digit NWIS parameter codes for streamflow (discharge) and gage height (stage).

phase_2.user_prompt: Now that we have the site and parameter codes, please retrieve the discrete field measurements (which contain paired stage and discharge data) over the 413 months beginning in August 1985.

phase_3.user_prompt: When working with field measurements, winter data is often affected by ice, which fundamentally alters the stage-discharge relationship. Filter the discrete measurements dataset to exclude any points where the channel control condition is flagged as ice-affected (e.g., control condition 'Ice cover' or explicit remarks noting shore ice that departs from the open-water rating). After removing these ice-affected records, how many valid open-water discrete measurements remain for our analysis period?

phase_4.user_prompt: To establish a baseline stage-discharge relationship across the entire study period, I want to fit a flexible curve to the open-water discrete measurements. Please fit a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) predicting the natural logarithm of discharge from stage, using a 5-knot cubic regression spline. What is the coefficient of determination (R-squared) of this fitted spline model? Finally, create a scatter plot of the discrete measurements (stage vs. log-discharge) overlaid with this fitted spline curve, and save it as `pere_marquette_spline_rating.png`.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The fitted cubic regression spline closely follows the non-linear, monotonically increasing relationship between stage and the logarithm of discharge throughout the period of record.
checkpoint.visual_description: A scatter plot with stage on one axis and discharge (or log-discharge) on the other. Individual points represent the filtered discrete field measurements. A smooth, continuous curve representing the 5-knot cubic regression spline should be overlaid, demonstrating a strong fit to the data points without excessive over-fitting.
